chapter: Fellow musicians: Kirk, Bunk, Parker, McShann
title: Why fame eluded the Thamon Hayes band
summary: Goodwin says the band was never in the right place at the right time despite being great.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well Baby, you and Crook might elaborate on this article I read in the Mississippi Rag that the banner headline said, "The Band that FAME Eluded" and the author of the article was writing about such a great band as Thamon Hayes and you were on it with Booker and the Walders but somehow or other fame eluded that band. Now why Baby?
You never got to the bigtime.
Well, I can't understand that to save
my life. I don't know what happened there because it just went down just "thump" like that, you know. I don't know why but --
We never were at the right place at the right time.
Well, you did go out on the road though.

We went out on the road and the people that were devoted to us; those that didn't run off with the money or something similar, well, it just looked like we were destined to fail but it was a great band.
But didn't you have a big chance in New York and you didn't take it?
We had a big chance right here in Kansas City.
